limitations: All records and mutations are deterministic synthetic fixtures; no operational cases or sources were used.
Citation checks verify identifier membership and output shape, not whether cited bytes semantically support a claim.
The legacy unanchored path accepts a full local rewrite; the opt-in HMAC receipt rejects it only while the key and receipt remain outside the attacker's control.
The file-backed HMAC adapter does not prevent rollback of an older signed receipt and is not an append-only remote anchor or immutable object store.
The report does not verify a deployed key manager, immutable storage, remote monotonic anchoring, publisher authorship, or hosted replay.

results.description: An exported synthetic evidence bundle verifies.
A local attacker rewrites bytes, the SQLite digest, and the unanchored ledger consistently.

A bundle contains an unlisted member.
A claim cites an evidence identifier in its allowed set.
A claim cites an identifier absent from its allowed set.
A clean ledger matches its external HMAC checkpoint.
The same local rewrite cannot replace an independent HMAC checkpoint.
An anchored bundle verifies with the external key provider.
A bundle receipt signature was altered.
A legacy bundle fails when the verifier requires an anchor.
